winner.title: Authentic Malagasy Romazava

evidence.authenticity: Beef chuck, ginger, garlic, tomato, paracress (anamalaho / brèdes mafane) added off heat to keep the tingle. Uses beef broth and a Dutch oven sear, which is Westernized. Author is not Malagasy. Context is a travel anecdote with little history.
evidence.precision: Weights on 3 of 11 ingredients (2.5 lb beef in 1.5-inch cubes, 1 lb paracress, 1/2 lb mustard greens). Doneness cues on most steps (deep brown crust, translucent onion, fork-tender beef, wilted greens). No pot size beyond 'large Dutch oven'.
evidence.testing: First-person trial-and-error anecdotes and one 'don't overcook the paracress' reason. No test notes. 4.71 rating from 7 votes.
evidence.photos: Schema lists an image on all 9 steps, but WebFetch of the page showed only a hero image. Scored on the mixed evidence.
evidence.efficiency: About 2h20m total. Searing and a 1.5 to 2 hour braise are reasonable, with no wasted steps.
evidence.access: Paracress is hard to find in the US. The page suggests arugula and mustard greens plus Szechuan peppercorn, and lists collards or mustard greens as the second green.

winner.why: It has the most doneness cues and sizing, and it handles the paracress tingle correctly, but it is a Westernized, SEO-style page and still falls short of 60.

runnerUp.title: Royal Romazava Recipe
runnerUp.source: Le Grand Bleu, Nosy Be (restaurant Le Turquoise)

evidence.authenticity: From a Madagascar restaurant. Zebu and chicken, brèdes, ginger, chilli. Little cultural context.
evidence.precision: Gram weights for the two meats only. Cues such as golden brown, translucent, meats tender, brèdes tender. Tomatoes and brèdes are not sized.
evidence.efficiency: About 1h30 total with no wasted steps.
evidence.access: Brèdes can be replaced with cassia leaves or local spinach.

runnerUp.why: It is more authentic in origin but gives fewer weights and cues than the winner.

candidates.disqualified: Not disqualified, but a 6.5 lb batch with no usable weights or cues.
Steps are paywalled and returned empty. Scored from the ingredients only, so it can't win.
No steps and weak amounts. Looks like generated content.

notes: No candidate reached 60. No test-kitchen recipe exists for romazava, and the sites search found nothing on Serious Eats, NYT, ATK or BBC Good Food. Most English pages are thin, time-only recipes. The Flavor365 site publishes several near-duplicate romazava pages, so treat it as a weak winner. The Von Diaz version (ckbk, from a cookbook) may be better, but its steps could not be read. The African Gourmet link from a search result returned 404 and was not used. Brèdes mafana (paracress) is hard to find in the US, so use arugula or mustard greens and add a little Szechuan peppercorn for the tingle.
